title: Split one axis through the section polynomial (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4488 assumes `||B|| ≤ 10 p^2`, `||C|| ≤ 10 p^2 + ε`, and `||B - C|| < 2 ε` on one axis, with `ε = p^6 exp(-p^2)`. What follows from splitting `B - C` through the section polynomial?

## Result

For vectors in a normed space,

```text
B - C = (B - P) + (P - C),
||B - C|| ≤ ||B - P|| + ||P - C||,
||P|| ≤ ||B|| + ||P - B||.
```

If both `||B - P||` and `||C - P||` are strictly below `ε`, then `||B - C|| < 2 ε`. If `||B|| ≤ 10 p^2` and `||P - B|| < ε`, then `||P|| < 10 p^2 + ε`.

The integer shadow uses errors of size 3: their sum is 6, and `6 < 2 · 4`. The polynomial norm with ceiling 10 and error 2 covers the sample value 6. Dropping the error fails, since `|13| > 10 + 1`.

**Claim type:** one triangle split. **No new κ.** Neither section error is proved, and the inverse ceiling is not derived. The tensor sum and the gate below `2^{-C p}` stay in #4488 and #4487. The #4100 notes are unchanged.

The locality audit already adds two `p^{10}` errors. This split is the same shape at `ε = p^6 exp(-p^2)`, together with the polynomial norm under the ceiling `10 p^2`.

This branch starts from canonical main. It does not replay #4488.
